source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: Which DOH-approved herbal medicine is used to clean wounds and as a mouthwash for swollen gums?
questions.rationale: Bayabas (Psidium guajava) leaves are boiled and used to clean wounds twice a day, or lukewarm as a mouthwash for mouth infections and swollen gums.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Herbal Medicine – Bayabas (PDF p. 98)
questions.quote: For cleansing or wounds, mouth infections and swollen gums

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: How should a client take bawang (garlic) to help lower cholesterol?
questions.rationale: For cholesterol, two cloves of garlic are eaten with meals three times a day. It may be sauteed, boiled, infused, or mixed with vinegar.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Herbal Medicine – Bawang (PDF p. 98–99)
questions.quote: Eat two clove of garlic with meals three times a day

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: A client with mild diabetes asks how to take ampalaya leaf decoction. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Two cups of chopped leaves are boiled in two glasses of water for 15 minutes on low fire; the client drinks ½ glass three times a day before eating.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Herbal Medicine – Ampalaya (PDF p. 99)
questions.quote: Drink ½ glass three times a day before eating

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.stem: Yerba buena is used for body pain. How is the decoction prepared?
questions.rationale: Chopped leaves are boiled in two glasses of water for 15 minutes without covering the pot, then cooled and strained. Fresh leaves may also be squeezed onto the painful part.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Herbal Medicine – Yerba Buena (PDF p. 97)
questions.quote: Cleanse thoroughly and chop the leaves, then boil in two glasses of water for 15 minutes.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which law strengthened Philippine disaster control capability and set up community disaster preparedness?
questions.rationale: PD 1566 (1978) strengthened the Philippine disaster control capability and established the National Program on Community Disaster Preparedness.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Health Emergency Preparedness and Response (PDF p. 99)
questions.quote: Presidential Decree No 1566 (1978) – Strengthening the Philippine Disaster Control Capability

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In disaster management, what is the FIRST priority?
questions.rationale: The first priority is protecting people at risk. The second is protecting the critical resources and systems communities depend on.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Health Emergency Preparedness and Response (PDF p. 99)
questions.quote: First priority: protection of the people who are at risk

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: A serious disruption causing losses that exceed the community's ability to cope with its own resources is a:
questions.rationale: A disaster is a serious disruption of a society causing widespread human, material, or environmental losses that exceed its ability to cope using its own resources. A hazard is a phenomenon with potential to cause damage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Disaster and Health Emergency Management (PDF p. 99)
questions.quote: exceed the ability of the affected society to cope, using only its own resources.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Population Groups
questions.situation: Nurse Ben is screening donors at a barangay blood-letting drive under the National Voluntary Blood Services Program (RA 7719).
questions.stem: What is the minimum weight to donate 450 mL of blood?
questions.rationale: Donors must weigh more than 45 kg for 250 mL and 50 kg (110 lb) for 450 mL of donated blood.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, National Voluntary Blood Services Program (PDF p. 100)
questions.quote: 50kg (110 lbs) for 450 ml of donated blood

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Population Groups
questions.situation: Nurse Ben is screening donors at a barangay blood-letting drive under the National Voluntary Blood Services Program (RA 7719).
questions.stem: A 17-year-old student wants to donate. What does Nurse Ben need?
questions.rationale: Donors may be 16 to 65 years old; those aged 16 and 17 need parental consent.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, National Voluntary Blood Services Program (PDF p. 100)
questions.quote: Be aged 16-65 years (for ages 16 & 17, parental consent is need)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Population Groups
questions.situation: Nurse Ben is screening donors at a barangay blood-letting drive under the National Voluntary Blood Services Program (RA 7719).
questions.stem: Which volunteer should Nurse Ben DEFER from donating?
questions.rationale: Contraindications include malaria, diabetes, cancer, heart disease, epilepsy, STIs, kidney or liver disease, and prohibited drug use. Hemoglobin must be at least 12.5 g/dL.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, National Voluntary Blood Services Program (PDF p. 100)
questions.quote: Malaria

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Health Education
questions.situation: Nurse Ben is screening donors at a barangay blood-letting drive under the National Voluntary Blood Services Program (RA 7719).
questions.stem: Which after-donation instruction should Nurse Ben give?
options: Carry heavy items with that arm
questions.rationale: After donating: keep the dressing on 3 to 12 hours, avoid heavy lifting with that arm, no smoking for 2 hours, no alcohol for 12 hours, and eat regular meals with more fluids.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, National Voluntary Blood Services Program (PDF p. 100)
questions.quote: Eat regular meals and increase fluid intake following your donation

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Whose commitment is required to supervise the operations of a Botika ng Barangay?
questions.rationale: A Botika ng Barangay requires a commitment from a licensed pharmacist to supervise its operations, plus at least 2 trained BHWs as aides.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Botika ng Barangay (PDF p. 101)
questions.quote: Commitment form a licensed pharmacist to supervise Botika ng Barangay operations

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: How much of a Botika ng Barangay's initial capital must come from the community?
questions.rationale: At least one-third of the initial capital must be community-sourced, and at least one-third from the LGU or other government officials.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Botika ng Barangay (PDF p. 101)
questions.quote: Community-sourced funds at least 1/3 of the initial capital requirements

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nursing students are starting a COPAR program in a depressed coastal barangay.
questions.stem: In which COPAR phase do the students select the site and do a preliminary social investigation?
questions.rationale: The pre-entry phase is done before going to the community: site selection criteria, site selection, preliminary social investigation, and networking with LGUs and NGOs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, COPAR Process (PDF p. 102)
questions.quote: Done before going to the community

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nursing students are starting a COPAR program in a depressed coastal barangay.
questions.stem: Which criterion should guide site selection for COPAR?
questions.rationale: Criteria: a socio-economically depressed, underserved community, inaccessible health services, poor health status, relative peace and order, and acceptance of the program.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, COPAR Process (PDF p. 102)
questions.quote: Health services are inaccessible

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nursing students are starting a COPAR program in a depressed coastal barangay.
questions.stem: The students live with the residents and share their hardships to build trust. Which COPAR activity is this?
questions.rationale: Integration is establishing rapport by immersing in community life and sharing the people's hopes and hardships to build mutual trust and cooperation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, 10 Critical Activities in COPAR (PDF p. 103)
questions.quote: Establishing rapport with the people in a continuing effort to imbibe community life

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nursing students are starting a COPAR program in a depressed coastal barangay.
questions.stem: The students go house to house, motivating residents one-on-one to act on an issue. What is this called?
questions.rationale: Ground working, also called agitation, means going around and motivating people one-on-one to do something about community issues.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, 10 Critical Activities in COPAR (PDF p. 103–104)
questions.quote: This entails going around and motivating people on a one-to-one basis to do something about community issues.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.situation: Nursing students are starting a COPAR program in a depressed coastal barangay.
questions.stem: Which criterion is used to choose core group members?
options: Respected and from the poor sector
questions.rationale: Core group members should be respected, from the poor sector, responsible and committed to social change, willing to learn, and able to communicate.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, COPAR Entry Phase (PDF p. 102)
questions.quote: Belongs to the poor sector of society

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: How are leaders identified in COPAR?
questions.rationale: COPAR is group-oriented, not leader-oriented. Leaders emerge and are tested through action rather than being appointed by an external entity.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, COPAR Principles (PDF p. 101)
questions.quote: Leaders are identified, emerge and are tested through action

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Utilization of Research
questions.stem: How does participatory action research differ from traditional research?
questions.rationale: In PAR, community members define the research problem as experts of their own reality and carry out the research, and the purpose is empowerment. In traditional research, external experts define and control it.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Participatory Action Research (PDF p. 104)
questions.quote: Research problems are defined by the community members themselves who are viewed as experts of their own reality
